vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: boilerplates
Version: 1.0.3

The skill bundle is a placeholder or skeleton for a boilerplate template collection based on a popular GitHub repository. The primary script, scripts/boilerplates.sh, contains only basic help and status commands with no functional logic implemented yet (marked as TODO), and there are no signs of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill claims to provide a collection of boilerplate templates but contains only a small helper script and documentation with the main 'run' functionality left unimplemented — it is misleading and not proportionate to its description.

dimensions.detail: The name/description promise a 'personal template collection' for many technologies, but the package only includes a short shell helper (prints help/info/status) and docs; no actual boilerplate templates or configurations are present. This mismatch is misleading: the requested/packaged artifacts do not align with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running a 'boilerplates' command and saving stdout; the included script only prints help/info/status and the 'run' command is a TODO. The instructions do not access environment variables, system files, or external endpoints beyond a static feedback URL — scope is limited but the functionality is unimplemented.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only with a bundled script). No external downloads or archive extraction are performed. This is low-risk from an install perspective.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. Nothing requests secrets or unrelated access — the credential footprint is minimal and proportional (in fact absent).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled, does not modify other skills or system-wide settings, and does not request persistent privileges. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default but there are no elevated privileges requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is misleading: it advertises a broad collection of boilerplates but only includes a small helper script and docs; the main 'run' functionality is unimplemented. It's low risk to run (no credentials, no external installs), but it's not useful as-is. Before installing or invoking: (1) inspect the files yourself — there are no hidden endpoints or secret accesses in the bundle; (2) do not expect real templates here — if you need boilerplates, fetch them directly from the referenced GitHub repo (ChristianLempa/boilerplates) or a trusted source; (3) avoid granting elevated privileges or integrating this automatically into workflows until the implementation actually provides the promised content. If you want this skill to be useful, ask the publisher for the actual templates or a working implementation of the 'run' command.
